claims.statement: Joseph Bertrand published the random chord paradox in Calcul des probabilités in 1889
Three well-specified random chord methods give 1/3, 1/2, 1/4 for longer than equilateral triangle side
The original shorter than side versions correspond to complementary probabilities; avoid swapping directions
The ambiguity concerns underspecified random-generating rules, not a formal contradiction among three theorems
Hilbert sixth problem in 1900 explicitly called for axiomatic treatment of probability and mechanics
Borel and later researchers developed the countable-additivity question on the way to Kolmogorov 1933
A countably additive distribution uniform on all positive integers cannot exist
Geometric distribution p(n)=2^-n over positive integers sums to one
Countable additivity distinguishes countable disjoint unions from finite additivity
Infinite independent fair binary trials have P(first occurrence at n)=2^-n and P(eventually occurs)=1
An individual infinite no-success path may be in the sample space yet have probability zero
For [0,1] uniform probability, decreasing events (0,1/n) have P=1/n→0 and empty intersection
The textbook sigma algebra/measure axioms must not be backdated to Bertrand 1889 or Borel 1898
